title: Probability Paths for Few-Step Generation
question: At a fixed training budget, design the probability path whose flow-matching model samples best at low NFE.
elab:
Probability paths with the same endpoints can differ in learning and discretization difficulty; the task designs paths that remain accurate when generation uses only a few Euler steps.

Flow matching regresses a velocity field along a conditional probability path from noise to data, and that path is two design choices: how noise and data samples are paired (independently, or by a minibatch optimal-transport plan) and how they are interpolated (linear optimal-transport, variance-preserving diffusion, trigonometric, stochastic interpolant). Together they determine how straight the learned flow is and therefore how well the model samples in few steps. The task trains a fixed 36M-parameter U-Net from scratch on CIFAR-10 and on ImageNet 32×32 (the datasets of Lipman et al. 2023) and scores FID on 50k samples with fixed-step Euler solvers at 8, 16 and 50 evaluations and with an adaptive dopri5 solver. It matters because the coupling and the path are fixed before training and cannot be recovered afterwards, so they are the decisions that set a model's few-step behaviour.
readme_settings_line: CIFAR-10 · 150k training steps · Euler 8/16/50 NFE; ImageNet 32×32 · 150k steps · Euler 8/16/50 NFE.
readme_methods_line: Independent linear path (Lipman et al., 2023); Minibatch OT-CFM (Tong et al., 2024); Stochastic interpolant (Albergo et al., 2023); VP trigonometric path (Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden, 2023); Reversed VP diffusion path (Lipman et al., 2023, eq. 19).
description_md:
# fm-probability-path

Which conditional probability path -- the coupling of noise and data samples
together with the interpolation between them -- gives the best flow-matching
image generator, above all when it must be sampled with few function
evaluations?

The fixed pipeline trains the same diffusers `UNet2DModel` (~35.7M parameters,
velocity head) from an identical seeded initialization on real image data with
the flow-matching velocity-regression objective. Noise-data coupling is
independent and training time is uniform. Optimizer, schedule, EMA, precision
and the update budget are fixed by the harness and identical for every path.

At each update the editable class sees an independently drawn noise batch
`x0` (Gaussian) and data batch `x1` (scaled to [-1, 1]). First
`ProbabilityPath.couple(x0, x1, generator)` chooses the minibatch coupling: it
returns two int64 index tensors `(i0, i1)` of shape `[B]` with values in
`[0, B)`, and training uses the pairs `(x0[i0], x1[i1])` (returning
`arange(B)` twice keeps the independent coupling). A fixed helper
`solve_assignment(cost)` solves an exact linear assignment on a `[B, B]` cost
tensor and returns the matched column per row. Then
`ProbabilityPath.sample(x0, x1, t, generator)` implements the complete
interpolation for the coupled pairs and its analytic time derivative, returning
`(x_t, dx_t)`; the network regresses `dx_t` from `(x_t, t)`. `t` is uniform in
[0, 1] and `generator` is an evaluator-owned CPU generator for any extra
randomness. It sees no model, optimizer, loss, training
step, evaluation handle, seed value, or other baseline and must remain
stateless. Outputs must be plain tensors of the endpoints' shape/device/dtype,
finite, and match `x(0)=x0`, `x(1)=x1` to 1% relative RMS (so a diffusion
schedule truncated at a small epsilon is admissible). The trained model is
sampled by integrating its velocity from `t=0` (noise) to `t=1` (data) in a
separate evaluation process that never imports the editable file.

The editable region must be exactly one `class ProbabilityPath` (methods, a
docstring and constant class attributes). It may call an allowlist of
`torch.<function>`s (elementwise math, reductions, `cdist`/`matmul`, tensor
construction and random sampling, `torch.linalg.vector_norm`/`norm`), public
`F.<function>` (`torch.nn.functional`) and `math.<function>` members, basic
builtins and `solve_assignment`; it may not import, reference other globals or
modules, touch private (`_`-prefixed) attributes, assign attributes, or keep
state. The runner rejects a violating region before training; the list of
allowed names is in `fm_path_common.py`.

After training, images are generated by integrating the learned ODE with both
fixed-step solvers at small function-evaluation budgets and an adaptive
high-accuracy solver, and each is scored by FID (lower is better). A fixed
velocity probe on the same path is an unscored diagnostic.

Reference baselines (all but `ot-cfm` keep the independent coupling):

- `linear` -- conditional-OT path, `x_t = (1-t) x0 + t x1`, `dx_t = x1 - x0`
  (Lipman, Chen, Ben-Hamu, Nickel & Le, "Flow Matching for Generative
  Modeling", ICLR 2023, Sec. 4.1 Example II). This is the unmodified starter.
- `vp-trigonometric` -- variance-preserving trigonometric path,
  `x_t = cos(pi t/2) x0 + sin(pi t/2) x1` (the trigonometric interpolant of
  Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden, ICLR 2023; `CosineScheduler` of
  facebookresearch/flow_matching).
- `vp-sde` -- the reversed variance-preserving diffusion path of Lipman et
  al. (eq. 19; `beta_min = 0.1`, `beta_max = 20`, time truncated at
  `1 - 1e-5` as in their App. E; `VPScheduler` of
  facebookresearch/flow_matching): `x_t = alpha_{1-t} x1 + sqrt(1 -
  alpha_{1-t}^2) x0`, `alpha_s = exp(-T(s)/2)`.
- `stochastic-interpolant` -- linear stochastic interpolant with a latent
  bridge, `x_t = (1-t) x0 + t x1 + gamma(t) z`, `gamma(t) = t(1-t)`,
  `z ~ N(0, I)` from the provided generator, `dx_t = x1 - x0 + gamma'(t) z`
  (Albergo, Boffi & Vanden-Eijnden, "Stochastic Interpolants: A Unifying
  Framework for Flows and Diffusions", arXiv:2303.08797, Table 8).

- `ot-cfm` -- minibatch optimal-transport coupling with the linear path
  (Tong, Malkin, Huguet, Zhang, Rector-Brooks, Fatras, Wolf & Bengio, "Improving
  and Generalizing Flow-Based Generative Models with Minibatch Optimal
  Transport", TMLR 2024, arXiv:2302.00482; torchcfm
  `ExactOptimalTransportConditionalFlowMatcher`, sigma = 0): exact OT plan
  between the noise and data minibatch under squared Euclidean cost, pairs
  resampled from the plan; see also Pooladian et al., "Multisample Flow
  Matching", ICML 2023 (BatchOT).

Lipman et al. report the conditional-OT path ahead of the VP diffusion path
(`vp-sde`) both with an adaptive solver and, by a wider margin, at low NFE.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Flow-matching training runner with an editable probability path (training phase).

The FIXED code trains one diffusers UNet2DModel (velocity head, parameter count
asserted) from an identical seeded initialization on unconditional image data
with the flow-matching velocity objective of the vendored
facebookresearch/flow_matching source.  Optimizer, schedule, EMA, precision and
the update budget are fixed and identical for every path.  This process only
trains and saves the EMA weights; a separate fixed evaluator (fm_path_eval.py,
a fresh interpreter that never imports this file) integrates the learned
velocity from t=0 (noise) to t=1 (data) with fixed-step and adaptive ODE
solvers and scores each solver by FID.  Coupling is independent, times uniform.
Only the probability path is editable.
Contract for ProbabilityPath (checked before it runs, see fm_path_common.py):
  * ``couple(x0, x1, generator)`` chooses the joint q(x0, x1) on the minibatch:
    it returns index tensors ``(i0, i1)`` (int64, shape [B], values in [0, B))
    and the pairs (x0[i0], x1[i1]) are trained on -- identity = independent
    coupling.  ``solve_assignment(cost)`` (exact linear assignment on a [B, B]
    cost, returns the matched column per row) is available as a fixed helper.
  * ``sample(x0, x1, t, generator)`` implements the complete interpolation and
    its analytic time derivative for the coupled pairs and returns ``(x_t, dx_t)``.
  * x0, x1: float32 [B, 3, H, W] on the training device (x1 in [-1, 1],
    x0 ~ N(0, I)); t: float32 [B], uniform in [0, 1]; generator: a CPU
    torch.Generator for any extra randomness.  The network regresses dx_t
    from (x_t, t) with a mean-squared error.
  * Outputs: plain tensors of the endpoints' shape/device/dtype, finite;
    x(0) and x(1) must match x0 and x1 to 1% relative RMS.
  * The region holds exactly one ``class ProbabilityPath`` (methods, a
    docstring and constant attributes only); it may use an allowlist of
    ``torch.<fn>`` callables, public ``F.<fn>`` / ``math.<fn>`` members, basic
    builtins and ``solve_assignment``; it must stay stateless and may not
    import, reach other globals, private attributes or modules.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math  # noqa: F401  (available to the editable region)
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F  # noqa: F401  (available to the editable region)

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
# The scoring pipeline points FM_PATH_TRUSTED_DIR at a root-owned, digest-checked
# copy of fm_path_common.py; standalone runs use the copy beside this file.
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ.get("FM_PATH_TRUSTED_DIR") or _HERE)
import fm_path_common as C  # noqa: E402

C.check_editable_file(__file__)  # static guard, runs before the class body executes
solve_assignment = C.solve_assignment  # fixed helper available to the editable class

# EDITABLE REGION START
class ProbabilityPath:
    """Independent coupling, linear conditional-OT interpolation and its analytic velocity."""

    def couple(self, x0, x1, generator):
        index = torch.arange(x0.shape[0], device=x0.device)
        return index, index

    def sample(self, x0, x1, t, generator):
        view = (t.shape[0],) + (1,) * (x0.ndim - 1)
        weight = t.view(view)
        x_t = (1.0 - weight) * x0 + weight * x1
        dx_t = x1 - x0
        return x_t, dx_t
# EDITABLE REGION END


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--dataset", choices=("cifar10", "imagenet32"), required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=150000)
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--ckpt-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--token", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--device", choices=("cuda", "cpu"), default="cuda")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.device == "cuda" and not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("a visible CUDA device is required")
    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True
    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True
    device = torch.device(args.device)
    images = C.load_train_images(args.dataset)
    path = ProbabilityPath()
    C.validate_endpoints(path, device)
    ema_model, train_loss, seconds, mean_time = C.train_model(
        args.steps, images, path, args.seed, args.batch, device)
    probe = C.probe_loss(ema_model, images, path, args.seed, device)
    C.write_checkpoint(args.ckpt_dir, args.token, ema_model, {
        "dataset": args.dataset, "seed": args.seed, "steps": args.steps,
        "train_loss": train_loss, "train_seconds": seconds, "train_time_mean": mean_time,
        "probe_vel_loss": probe})
    print(f"TRAIN_DONE: steps={args.steps} train_loss={train_loss:.6f} probe={probe:.6f} "
          f"seconds={seconds:.1f} upstream=facebookresearch/flow_matching@{C.FLOW_MATCHING_COMMIT}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        "dataset": args.dataset, "seed": args.seed, "steps": args.steps,
        "train_loss": train_loss, "train_seconds": seconds, "train_time_mean": mean_time,
        "probe_vel_loss": probe})
    print(f"TRAIN_DONE: steps={args.steps} train_loss={train_loss:.6f} probe={probe:.6f} "
          f"seconds={seconds:.1f} upstream=facebookresearch/flow_matching@{C.FLOW_MATCHING_COMMIT}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
